\section{Statements of results}\label{sec:statements}
\begin{lemma}[Strict positivity preservation]\label{lem:pos}
If $P$ is a stochastic matrix with strictly positive entries and $v\ge 0$ is nonzero, then $Pv > 0$ componentwise.
\end{lemma}
\begin{theorem}[Spectral gap for positive stochastic matrices]\label{thm:gap}
Every strictly positive $n\times n$ stochastic matrix $P$ has simple eigenvalue $1$ and all other eigenvalues satisfy $|\lambda| < 1$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{corollary}[Exponential mixing]\label{cor:mix}
There exist $C>0$ and $\rho\in(0,1)$ such that $\|P^k \mu - \pi\|_1 \le C \rho^k$ for every probability vector $\mu$.
\end{corollary}
\section{Proofs}\label{sec:proofs}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:pos}]
Each entry $(Pv)_i = \sum_j P_{ij} v_j$ is a sum of nonnegative terms with at least one strictly positive term.
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem 1.2]
By Birkhoff's contraction in the Hilbert projective metric, the positive cone maps strictly inside itself, forcing uniqueness of the unit eigenvector.
\end{proof}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:mix} \cite{seneta2006}]
Expand $P^k \mu$ in the Jordan basis and apply the spectral bound $|\lambda| < 1$ on the subspace orthogonal to the invariant measure.
\end{proof}
\section{A short remark with attached proof}\label{sec:attached}
\begin{proposition}[Row sum invariance]\label{prop:rowsum}
The all-ones vector $\mathbf{1}$ satisfies $P^k \mathbf{1} = \mathbf{1}$ for every $k\ge 1$.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Induction on $k$ using $P\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}$.
\end{proof}
